data.title: Greater Flamingo Flocks Gather Along Al-Lith Coast
data.content:
Jeddah, November 22, 2026, SPA -- Large flocks of greater flamingos have gathered along the Red Sea coast of Al-Lith Governorate, bringing a touch of pink to its shallow coastal waters. The birds, with their white plumage tinged with pink and distinctive long necks, were seen wading close to shore.
    The Saudi Press Agency (SPA) captured images of some flamingos wading through the water on their long pink legs, while others stood in scattered groups. Several birds were also photographed taking flight from the water at nearly the same time.
    Prof. Khalid Ali Asiry of King Abdulaziz University's Faculty of Environmental Sciences told SPA that the greater flamingo, locally known as "fenteer," is a migratory bird that visits the Red Sea coast. Its numbers typically increase during autumn and winter, although some birds may remain in the area for longer periods of the year.
    Asiry explained that the ebb and flow of the tides expose mudflats and shallow-water areas along the Al-Lith coast, providing ideal feeding grounds for flamingos. Using their curved bills, the birds filter small crustaceans, algae, and microorganisms from the water and mud. Quiet coastal areas also provide places for them to rest along their migratory journey.
    Flamingos are social birds that gather wherever food is available. Changes in water levels may also prompt large numbers to move to a single location, Asiry noted. However, comparing the number of birds currently observed in Al-Lith with those recorded in previous years would require monitoring data beyond what is currently available.
    Asiry stressed the importance of protecting coastal sites used by migratory birds for feeding and resting, minimizing disturbances, and regularly monitoring their numbers. Such efforts, he said, are essential to understanding how changing environmental conditions affect their migration and gathering patterns.
    -- SPA
